item.text: I’m changing the connected-components API now so callers use a dedicated result object instead of raw nested lists. That will shrink knowledge of the internal list shape to one place and give the app/tests a cleaner seam.

There’s a small follow-up edit: the new result-immutability check needs to be wired into the test entrypoint, and the test file still needs `List` imported for the invalid graph fixture. I’m fixing that before verification.
The result object refactor is in place. I’m compiling and running both the demo and the tests now to confirm the new API boundary didn’t break behavior.
Verification passed. I’m grabbing the updated line references so the summary can point to the API changes directly instead of just naming files.

The main refactor here was replacing the raw `List<List<Integer>>` return shape with a dedicated result type. [ConnectedComponentsResult.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/027_connected_components/ConnectedComponentsResult.java:5) now owns the immutable snapshot of the traversal output, exposes `componentCount()`, provides the formatted output, and centralizes the string representation. That removes nested-list knowledge from callers.

[GraphComponentFinder.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/027_connected_components/GraphComponentFinder.java:12) now returns that result object directly and passes the validated vertex count through the traversal path instead of repeatedly reaching back into the graph. [ConnectedComponents.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/027_connected_components/ConnectedComponents.java:6) is correspondingly simpler, and [ConnectedComponentsTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/027_connected_components/ConnectedComponentsTest.java:8) now checks the new public API, including result immutability.

Verified with `javac *.java`, `java ConnectedComponents`, and `java ConnectedComponentsTest`.
